verdict: Dollar Tree grew sales 7% to $4.9B, and a $383M tariff-refund windfall — worth $1.31 of its $2.70 in earnings per share — turned a solid quarter into a blowout one.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Net sales were $4,887M, vs $4,567M a year ago (continuing operations)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $0.75 a year ago from continuing operations — includes a $1.31 tariff-refund benefit

kpis.label: Same-store sales
kpis.note: Average ticket up 3.3%, traffic up 0.4% — on top of +6.5% a year ago

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash from operations of $922M less $246M of store investment, from continuing operations

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in 9,436 Dollar Tree and Dollar Tree Canada stores. Same-store sales rose 3.7%, and 75 new stores opened in the quarter.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Small fees and other income on top of store sales.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores and the company — pay, rent and marketing. The reported SG&A bill was $1,427M; this line nets off $18M of transition-services income received for supporting Family Dollar after its sale.

otherDetail: Other income of $14M — interest earned on tariff refunds — mostly offset $18M of net interest expense: a net $3M cost after rounding.
follow100Note: The rows add to $100.01 due to rounding. Profit is income from continuing operations — Dollar Tree sold Family Dollar in 2025, so there were no discontinued operations this quarter.

takeaways.title: A tariff refund super-sized the quarter
takeaways.text: Refunds of IEEPA tariffs (import taxes later refunded) totaled $383M — $369M credited against the cost of goods and $14M of interest. After $37M spent reinvesting the windfall and $13M of extra duties, the net benefit was $1.31 of the $2.70 EPS. Gross margin jumped 850 basis points to 42.9%, with 680 of those points from the refunds.

takeaways.title: Shoppers spent more per trip
takeaways.text: Same-store sales rose 3.7% on top of 6.5% a year ago: the average ticket grew 3.3% and traffic 0.4%. About 6,600 stores now use the multi-price format, and 75 new stores opened, taking the chain to 9,436 stores.

takeaways.title: Cash is going back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Dollar Tree bought back $605M of its own stock in the quarter (5.6M shares) and still ended with $1.1B of cash and no borrowings drawn. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $7.70–$8.05, including about $0.60 from the tariff refunds.

oneTimers: Tariff refunds: $383M of IEEPA tariff refunds ($369M in cost of sales, $14M of interest income), partly offset by $22M of reinvestment costs in cost of sales, $15M in SG&A, and $13M of duties on aluminum pans and paper plates — a net benefit of $1.31 per diluted share. Excluding the net impact, EPS would have been about $1.39.
All figures are from continuing operations (the Dollar Tree and Dollar Tree Canada banners). Family Dollar, sold on July 5, 2025, sits in discontinued operations in the prior-year quarter only.
footerNote: Continuing operations throughout: prior-year comparisons exclude Family Dollar, which was sold in 2025. Figures are rounded to $M; net sales absorbs a $1M rounding difference so segment lines add exactly to total revenue.
